mainTopic: Whether blood on a checking cloth makes a woman a definite נדה, the dispute of רבי and רבי יוסי, and the משנה's time frames ('immediately', 'after some time') for blood found after relations
overview: The גמרא finishes the exchange between רבי חייא and רבי about blood found later on a checking cloth. It concludes that in his youth רבי חייא ruled the woman a full נדה. Next comes a story: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי meets רבי חמא בר ביסא. He is surprised that רבי חמא prefers רבי's view over that of רבי יוסי, who was רבי's teacher. The גמרא explains that רבי's rulings were sharpened by the many חכמים in his yeshiva. A ברייתא shows that in the unchecked-cloth case רבי says טמאה and רבי יוסי says טהורה. רבי זירא links each view to the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי about blood seen while urinating. The גמרא then returns to our משנה. It defines 'immediately' with the doorpost picture and explains why our משנה requires no אשם תלוי. Finally, it works through the contradiction about how long 'after some time' is. רב חסדא and רב אשי each give an answer, and a ברייתא from אושא begins a challenge to רב אשי that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי חייא argues that רבי is really treating the blood as a stain
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא gets רבי to agree that the blood must be more than a split bean, then argues that this means רבי is treating it as a כתם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said to רבי: Don't you agree that she is only טמאה if the blood is more than the size of a split bean? רבי said: Yes. רבי חייא said: Then you are also treating it as a כתם.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא challenges רבי's ruling. He first gets רבי to admit one point, then uses it against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The size rule (more than a split bean) is a rule that belongs to כתמים, stains whose טומאה comes only from doubt. If the blood surely came from her body, any amount should count. So רבי חייא argues that needing a minimum size shows רבי himself is only treating this blood as a doubtful stain.

keyTerms.meaning: More than the size of a split bean, the minimum size for a stain to make a woman טמאה
A blood stain found on a garment or cloth. It makes a woman טמאה only out of doubt (מדרבנן)
Here: 'Yes, indeed', a word of agreement
If so, used to draw a conclusion from what was just admitted

steps.confusionAlert: Here אֲבָל does not mean 'but.' In this line it means 'yes, indeed.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי, who had just ruled that the woman is definitely טמאה.

phrases.english: Do you not concede
that she requires more than a split bean?
phrases.notes: He means the blood on the cloth must be bigger than a split bean before she becomes טמאה.

phrases.english: He said to him: Indeed.
He said to him: If so,
you too have made it a stain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי חִיָּיא: אִי אַתָּה מוֹדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story in which רבי ruled the woman definitely טמאה because of blood found later on her checking cloth.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's ruling that the woman is definitely טמאה as a נדה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Requiring a minimum size is a rule for כתמים. If רבי needs that size too, he is really treating the blood as a doubtful stain and not as certain נדה blood.

steps.title: Why רבי still holds the woman is definitely טמאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that for רבי, the size rule only rules out louse blood. Once that is ruled out, the blood surely came from her body.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי holds: we need more than a split bean only to rule out that it is the blood of a louse. Once louse blood is ruled out, the blood surely came from her body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי's side, so we see why רבי חייא's argument does not force him to change his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא saw the size rule as proof that the case is only a doubt. רבי sees it as a way of removing one specific doubt, that a squashed louse made the blood. Once that doubt is gone, nothing is left to doubt, so for רבי she is definitely טמאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of a louse, which could make a small stain
To exclude or rule out
Certainly, definitely
We require

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the same size rule can be read two ways. רבי חייא reads it as a sign of doubt, and רבי reads it as a tool that removes doubt.

phrases.english: And Rabbi holds:
We require 'more than a split bean'
to exclude the blood of a louse,
and since it has been excluded from being louse blood,
it certainly came from her body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי's reasoning in response to רבי חייא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the purpose of the size requirement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The size requirement shows the blood is only treated as a doubtful כתם.
steps.terutzMaskana: The size requirement only rules out louse blood. After that, the blood is certainly from her body, so she is definitely טמאה.

steps.title: Proof that in his youth רבי חייא ruled her טמאה as a נדה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that רבי חייא argued this way in his old age. Here he treats the blood as only a כתם, so in his youth he must have ruled she is definitely a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this exchange from the time of old age? So it must be that in his youth he ruled her טמאה as a נדה. Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the exchange to settle the earlier question about the order of רבי חייא's rulings. It concludes that in his youth רבי חייא ruled she is definitely a נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was whether רבי חייא's ruling of 'נדה' came in his youth or in his old age. A student would argue with his great teacher like this only in his later years, and here רבי חייא treats the blood as a כתם. So his 'נדה' ruling must be the earlier one, from his youth.

keyTerms.meaning: In his old age
In his youth
Ruled her definitely טמאה as a menstruating woman
Learn from this, a proof is accepted
Is it not so that…? A question that introduces a proof

steps.whatToRemember: The conclusion: in his youth רבי חייא ruled the woman definitely טמאה as a נדה. In his old age, as in this exchange with רבי, he ruled her טמאה only because of כתם.

phrases.english: What, is it not that he was standing in his old age?
Hence in his youth he deemed her impure as a menstruating woman!
Conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the exchange in steps 1-2 to answer the earlier question about the order of רבי's rulings.
steps.raayaObject: The question of whether רבי חייא's 'נדה' ruling came in his youth or in his old age
steps.raayaSupportSource: The exchange between רבי חייא and רבי, which happened in the later years
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In his youth רבי חייא ruled טמאה משום נדה, and in his old age טמאה משום כתם.

steps.title: רבי praises רבי חמא בר ביסא to רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins. רבי praises רבי חמא בר ביסא as a great man, and רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי asks to meet him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי praised רבי חמא בר ביסא to רבי ישמעאל the son of רבי יוסי, saying he is a great man. רבי ישמעאל said: When he comes to you, bring him to me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new story. It sets the scene for a meeting that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far this is only the setup: the praise and the request to meet. What happens at the meeting, and how it connects to our topic, comes in the following lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Praised, spoke highly of
A great man, a great scholar
When he comes to you, literally 'into your hand'

phrases.english: Rabbi would praise
to Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei
about Rabbi Chama bar Bisa,
phrases.notes: This בְּרַבִּי does not mean 'son of' like the one before it. Here it means 'about רבי', telling us who was praised.

phrases.english: that he is a great man.
He said to him: When he comes to you,
bring him to me.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשְׁתַּבַּח לֵיהּ רַבִּי לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new story after the earlier question has been settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This sets up the meeting between רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי and רבי חמא בר ביסא.

steps.title: רבי חמא asks about blood found later on an unchecked cloth
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל invites רבי חמא to ask a question. רבי חמא asks about a woman who checked herself with an unchecked cloth, put it in a box, and found blood on it the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי חמא came, רבי ישמעאל said to him: Ask me something. He asked: A woman checked herself with a cloth that she had not checked beforehand. She put it in a box, and the next day she found blood on it. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: רבי חמא arrives, and רבי ישמעאל invites him to ask a halachic question. רבי חמא asks about blood found on an unchecked cloth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cloth was never checked before she used it, so the blood could have been on it from before. She also only found the blood the next day. The question is whether she counts as a נדה, and this sets up the disagreement between רבי יוסי and רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: A cloth a woman uses to check herself for blood
That was not checked beforehand to make sure it was clean
A box
What is the law?

phrases.english: When he came, he said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי חמא is the one who came, and רבי ישמעאל is the one speaking.

phrases.english: Ask me something.
He asked him:
A woman checked herself with a cloth that she had not checked beforehand,
and she put it in a box,
and the next day she found blood on it. What is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from Step 4, where רבי ישמעאל asked to meet רבי חמא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a woman is a נדה when blood is found the next day on a cloth that was not checked before use.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל offers two opinions, and רבי חמא chooses רבי
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל asks whether he should answer according to his father רבי יוסי or according to רבי. רבי חמא asks for רבי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said to him: Should I tell you the answer according to my father, or according to רבי? He said: Tell me according to רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: Before answering, רבי ישמעאל offers a choice between two opinions: his father רבי יוסי's and רבי's. רבי חמא picks רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל signals that רבי יוסי and רבי disagree about this case. The real point of the story is which opinion רבי חמא chooses, because that choice sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the words or opinion of
Father. Here it means רבי ישמעאל's father, רבי יוסי

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: כְּדִבְרֵי אַבָּא אֵימָא לָךְ,
phrases.english: He said to him: Should I tell you according to the words of Father,
phrases.notes: "Father" is רבי יוסי, since the speaker is רבי ישמעאל the son of רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: or should I tell you according to the words of רבי?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּדִבְרֵי רַבִּי אֵימָא לִי.
phrases.english: He said to him: Tell me according to the words of רבי.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִבְרֵי אַבָּא אֵימָא לָךְ אוֹ כְּדִבְרֵי רַבִּי אֵימָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי חמא's question by offering a choice of two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No ruling is given yet. רבי ישמעאל offers two opinions, and רבי חמא chooses רבי's.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל is shocked that רבי חמא prefers the student over the teacher
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל asks how this can be the great man רבי praised, if he passes over the teacher, רבי יוסי, to follow the student, רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said: Is this the one people say is a great man? How can someone leave the words of the teacher and listen to the words of the student?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל challenges רבי חמא's choice. רבי יוסי was רבי's teacher, so how can anyone follow the student over the teacher?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption behind the challenge is that a teacher's view should carry more weight than his student's. Because רבי חמא did the opposite, רבי ישמעאל questions whether he deserves the praise רבי gave him in Step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: A great man
The teacher, here רבי יוסי
The student, here רבי

phrases.english: רבי ישמעאל said:

phrases.aramaic: זֶהוּ שֶׁאוֹמְרִין עָלָיו דְּאָדָם גָּדוֹל הוּא?
phrases.english: Is this the one they say is a great man?
phrases.notes: This points back to Step 4, where רבי praised רבי חמא as a great man.

phrases.english: How can one leave aside the words of the teacher
and listen to the words of the student?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיאַךְ מַנִּיחִין דִּבְרֵי הָרַב וְשׁוֹמְעִין דִּבְרֵי הַתַּלְמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי חמא's choice in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חמא's choice to follow רבי rather than רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teacher should be followed over his student. רבי יוסי was רבי's teacher, so choosing רבי seems backwards.

steps.title: Why רבי חמא chose רבי: debate at the head of the yeshiva sharpens rulings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי חמא held that רבי heads the yeshiva and many חכמים are often with him, so his rulings get sharpened through discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חמא בר ביסא held: רבי is the head of the yeshiva, and the חכמים are often in front of him, and they sharpen his teachings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי חמא's choice by explaining his reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חמא did not think the student always wins. His point is that רבי's rulings are constantly tested by many חכמים in the yeshiva, which makes them sharper and more reliable. That answers רבי ישמעאל's challenge that a teacher must always be followed over his student.

keyTerms.meaning: Head of the yeshiva
The חכמים are often in front of him
His teachings become sharp

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חמא followed רבי over his teacher רבי יוסי because a ruling tested by many חכמים in the yeshiva becomes sharper and more reliable.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי חמא is not saying a student is greater than his teacher. He is saying that constant debate in the yeshiva makes רבי's rulings sharper.

phrases.english: And רבי חמא בר ביסא held:
רבי is the head of the yeshiva,
and the חכמים are often in front of him,
and his teachings are sharpened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ישמעאל's challenge in Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the reasoning behind the choice that was challenged.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A teacher's opinion should always be followed over his student's.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי's rulings are tested by many חכמים in his yeshiva, so they are sharper and can be preferred even over his teacher's.

steps.title: What were the two opinions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the rulings of רבי and רבי יוסי were in the case of the unchecked cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did רבי say, and what did רבי יוסי say?
steps.whatsHappening: The story mentioned two possible answers, one by רבי and one by רבי יוסי, without telling us what they were. Now the גמרא asks what each of them actually ruled. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, רבי ישמעאל offered to answer either like his father רבי יוסי or like רבי. The story never told us their actual rulings. So the גמרא stops the story to fill in that missing information.

keyTerms.meaning: What is; used to ask for the content or meaning of something

phrases.english: What is the view of Rabbi, and what is the view of Rabbi Yosei?
phrases.notes: This is about the cloth case in step 5, where רבי ישמעאל offered both views.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the story to ask what the two opinions in it were.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The actual rulings of רבי and רבי יוסי regarding blood found on an unchecked cloth placed in a box.

steps.title: רבי says impure, רבי יוסי says pure
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנא quotes a ברייתא: רבי rules the woman טמאה, and רבי יוסי rules her טהורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנא said: a ברייתא teaches that רבי says she is impure, and רבי יוסי says she is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר מתנא answers the question by quoting a ברייתא. רבי says the woman is טמאה, and רבי יוסי says she is טהורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know the dispute. רבי treats the blood on the cloth as coming from the woman, even though the cloth was never checked beforehand. רבי יוסי does not make her impure, since the blood may have been on the cloth before she used it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rules that someone or something is impure (טמא)
Rules that someone or something is pure (טהור)

steps.confusionAlert: Remember that רבי חמא chose רבי's view, the stricter one, even though רבי יוסי was the older teacher. That is what bothered רבי ישמעאל in step 7.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana said:
It was taught: Rabbi deems her impure,
and Rabbi Yosei deems her pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא, תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 directly.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to a ברייתא, רבי rules the woman טמאה and רבי יוסי rules her טהורה.

steps.title: Each view fits a bigger approach
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that רבי's strict ruling follows רבי מאיר, while רבי יוסי's lenient ruling follows his own known approach.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: When רבי ruled her impure, he followed רבי מאיר. When רבי יוסי ruled her pure, he followed his own view.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא adds that these two rulings are not random. Each one matches an approach we already know from elsewhere. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי is not inventing a new strict idea. He is following the reasoning of רבי מאיר. רבי יוסי is being consistent with something he himself says in another case. רבי זירא is connecting this dispute to an older מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with the reasoning of רבי מאיר
For himself; following his own established view

phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira said:
When Rabbi deemed her impure, it was in line with Rabbi Meir,
and when Rabbi Yosei deemed her pure, he deemed her pure according to his own view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the dispute identified in step 10 by tracing each side to a wider approach.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי's strict view follows the reasoning of רבי מאיר, while רבי יוסי's lenient view is consistent with his own reasoning elsewhere.

steps.title: The case of blood seen while urinating
steps.stepSummary: A source is brought: when a woman sees blood while urinating, רבי מאיר says standing is טמאה and sitting is טהורה, while רבי יוסי says she is טהורה either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: A woman was urinating and saw blood. רבי מאיר says: if she was standing, she is impure. If she was sitting, she is pure. רבי יוסי says: either way, she is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that proves רבי זירא's claim. It is an earlier מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי about blood seen while urinating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When she stands, the blood could have come from the womb, and רבי מאיר makes her טמאה even though it might be from the urinary tract. רבי יוסי makes her טהורה in both cases, because there is a real doubt about where the blood came from. In the same way, רבי makes her impure despite the doubt about the cloth, like רבי מאיר, and רבי יוסי makes her pure because of the doubt, as he does here.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'doing her needs'; a polite way of saying urinating
Standing
Sitting
Either way; in both cases

steps.whatToRemember: רבי follows רבי מאיר and is strict even when the blood might have come from somewhere else. רבי יוסי is consistently lenient when there is a real doubt about where the blood came from.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the cloth dispute is part of a bigger question: how much weight should a doubt about the blood's source carry in הלכות נדה?

phrases.english: As it is taught: A woman who was urinating
and saw blood,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אִם עוֹמֶדֶת — טְמֵאָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: If she was standing, she is impure,
if she was sitting, she is pure.
Rabbi Yosei says:
Whether this way or that way, she is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָיְתָה עוֹשָׂה צְרָכֶיהָ וְרָאֲתָה דָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that backs up רבי זירא's claim in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רבי זירא's claim that רבי follows רבי מאיר and that רבי יוסי follows his own view.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי about a woman who sees blood while urinating: רבי מאיר says standing is טמאה and sitting is טהורה, while רבי יוסי says she is טהורה either way.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי מאיר made her impure only because of a stain
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא challenges רב אשי. According to רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, רבי מאיר made her טמאה only because of a כתם, while רבי rules she is a full נדה. So how can רבי's ruling follow רבי מאיר?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רבא, said to רב אשי: But didn't רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא say that when רבי מאיר made her impure, he did so only because of a stain? Yet רבי is saying she is impure as a נדה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the claim from step 11 that רבי's strict ruling follows רבי מאיר. A statement is quoted showing that the two rulings are not the same kind of impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says רבי מאיר's impurity in the urine case is only a weaker, doubtful impurity, the level of a כתם. But רבי rules that the woman with the unchecked cloth is a full, definite נדה. A weaker ruling cannot be the source for a stronger one, so the link between them seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But surely…'. Opens a challenge from a known source.
A blood stain. Its impurity is a lighter, rabbinic level, not full נדה.
A woman who is definitely impure from menstrual blood (the full Torah-level status).
'Whereas'. Sets up a contrast between two things.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, say,
when Rabbi Meir made her impure
phrases.notes: This is the case from step 12: the woman who sees blood while urinating standing up.

phrases.english: he made her impure only because of a stain,
whereas Rebbi is saying she is impure as a niddah!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the step 11 link, which step 12 had backed up.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי's ruling in the unchecked-cloth case follows רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר's impurity is only at the level of a כתם, but רבי's is full נדה. The two rulings are different in strength, so one cannot be based on the other.

steps.title: The statement actually said רבי מאיר rules she is a נדה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that when רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's statement was said, it said רבי מאיר made her impure as a נדה, not just because of a כתם.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is how we say it: when that statement was said, it was said as 'because of נדה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends the link by correcting the wording of the quoted statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי says his version of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's statement is different. In his version, רבי מאיר makes her a full נדה. Now רבי מאיר and רבי are at the same level of strictness, and the link from step 11 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what we say'. Introduces the speaker's own version of a teaching.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is how we say it:
phrases.notes: רב אשי is answering רב אחא.

phrases.english: when that statement was said,
it was said as 'because of niddah.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different version of the quoted statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר's impurity is only because of a כתם, so רבי cannot follow him.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר rules she is a full נדה, so רבי's ruling can follow him.
steps.whatToRemember: In the end, רבי's strict ruling still follows רבי מאיר, because רבי מאיר also makes her a full נדה.

steps.title: How short is 'immediately'? The doorpost picture
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's case of blood found 'immediately' after relations. A ברייתא explains with a picture: the cloth goes in just as the organ comes out, like two people at a doorway.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If blood was found on her cloth immediately, they are impure, etc. The רבנן taught: What is the time frame for the period? It is like an organ and a cloth standing at the side of the doorpost: as the organ goes out, the cloth comes in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא that defines exactly how fast 'immediately' must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, blood found 'immediately' makes both husband and wife definitely impure, and both must bring a חטאת. The ברייתא says this applies only when there is no gap at all: the cloth must enter as the organ leaves. Only then can we be sure the bleeding started during the relations.

keyTerms.meaning: Immediately, right away.
The amount of time for the onset of the period (here, what counts as 'immediately').
Literally 'attendant'. A polite word for the male organ.
Literally 'witness'. The checking cloth.
Doorpost. Here a picture word for the entrance of the body.

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא עַל שֶׁלָּהּ אוֹתְיוֹם טְמֵאִין וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: If blood was found on her cloth immediately, they are impure, etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from our משנה: both are impure and each brings a חטאת.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: What is the time frame for the period?
It is like an organ and a cloth
standing at the side of the doorpost,
as the organ goes out, the cloth comes in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Immediately' means the cloth enters as the organ leaves, with no gap at all.

steps.title: This time frame is for wiping, not a full check
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that this very short time frame was said about an outside wipe. It was not said about a full internal check, which takes too long.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the time frame they spoke of: for wiping, but not for an examination.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the rule from the ברייתא: it only works with a quick outside wipe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A quick wipe can happen with no gap, so blood found that way counts as 'immediately.' A full internal check takes longer, so the time passes and we can no longer be sure the blood came during relations. That case would not get the 'immediately' ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Wiping: a quick outside wipe with the cloth.
Examination: a full internal check, which takes more time.

phrases.english: This is the time frame they spoke of
for wiping, but not for an examination.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the definition given in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'immediately' time frame works only with an outside wipe, not with a full internal check.
steps.whatToRemember: 'Immediately' means no gap at all, and only a quick wipe can be that fast.

steps.title: 'After time': a ברייתא adds an אשם תלוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of blood found after some time passed. A ברייתא teaches that in this case each of them must bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If blood was found on her cloth after some time, etc. It was taught: And they are obligated to bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא that adds an extra rule not stated in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, when time has passed, the couple is only impure because of a doubt, and they do not bring a חטאת. The ברייתא adds that since they may have sinned, each must bring an אשם תלוי, the offering brought when someone is unsure whether he did a sin that needs a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: After some time has passed.
A 'hanging' guilt offering, brought when one is unsure whether he did a sin that needs a חטאת.

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא עַל שֶׁלָּהּ לְאַחַר זְמַן וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: If blood was found on her cloth after some time, etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from our משנה: they are impure only because of a doubt, and they do not bring a חטאת.

phrases.english: It was taught: And they are obligated to bring a provisional guilt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה after finishing the 'immediately' case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When blood is found after some time, each of them must bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two offerings: a חטאת is for a sin we know happened, and an אשם תלוי is for a sin that might have happened.

steps.title: Why doesn't our משנה require an אשם תלוי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the reason is for our משנה, which does not mention any אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא of our משנה, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why our משנה leaves out the אשם תלוי that the ברייתא requires. This question sets up the next move, and the next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the couple brings an אשם תלוי, but our משנה only says they are exempt from a חטאת. The question is what reason the תנא of our משנה has for not requiring an אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Our תנא': the author of our משנה.
'What is the reason?'

phrases.english: And the tanna of our mishnah, what is his reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why doesn't our משנה require an אשם תלוי, the way the ברייתא does?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the gap between the ברייתא in step 17 and our משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason our משנה does not require an אשם תלוי in the 'after time' case.

steps.title: An אשם תלוי needs a doubt between two pieces
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה holds that an אשם תלוי is only brought when there was a doubt between two pieces, one forbidden and one permitted. That is not the case here.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need a case of one piece out of two pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 18: why does our משנה not require an אשם תלוי? The answer is that an אשם תלוי needs a 'one piece out of two pieces' kind of doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The classic case for an אשם תלוי is two pieces of meat, one forbidden and one permitted, where a person ate one and does not know which. Here there is only one woman, and the doubt is whether relations with her were permitted at all. Because no forbidden item was clearly there to begin with, our משנה holds that no אשם תלוי is brought. This is different from the ברייתא in step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: We need / we require
One piece out of two pieces: a doubt where one item is surely forbidden and one surely permitted
A 'hanging' guilt offering, brought when a person is unsure whether he did a sin

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה holds that an אשם תלוי needs a 'one piece out of two pieces' doubt. A doubt about one single item is not enough.
steps.confusionAlert: The text here is very short. It never mentions the woman or the אשם תלוי directly. It assumes you remember the question from step 18.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the disagreement between our משנה and the ברייתא in step 17. The ברייתא requires an אשם תלוי even in a single-item doubt.

phrases.english: We require one piece out of two pieces.
phrases.notes: Picture two pieces of meat, one forbidden and one permitted, and you ate one without knowing which. Our case has only one 'piece', the one woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An אשם תלוי is only brought for a doubt like 'one piece out of two pieces'. A doubt about a single woman does not qualify.

steps.title: A ברייתא defines 'after some time' as a shorter time
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines 'after some time' as long enough to get out of bed and rinse. A ברייתא of רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק defines it as only long enough to reach under the pillow for a cloth and check.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה asks what counts as 'after some time,' and so on. The גמרא points to a contradiction: what counts as 'after some time'? רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק explained that it is the time it takes her to reach her hand under the pillow or the blanket, take a cloth, and check with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's definition of 'after some time.' It then sets against it a ברייתא that gives a much shorter definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, 'after some time' means the time to get out of bed and rinse herself. In the ברייתא, it means only the few seconds needed to reach under the pillow for a cloth. The same phrase seems to be defined in two different ways, so the two sources seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: And he set them against each other: the גמרא is pointing out a contradiction between two sources
After some time: the משנה's second time frame for finding blood
Pillow or cushion / blanket
A checking cloth used to check for blood

phrases.english: What is 'after some time,' etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. The rest of the line is: long enough to get down from the bed and rinse.

phrases.english: And a contradiction was raised: what is 'after some time'?
Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Tzadok explained:
Enough time for her to reach out her hand
under the pillow or under the blanket
and take a cloth and check with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: how long the משנה's 'after some time' is
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's definition of 'after some time' as getting out of bed and rinsing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא defines the same phrase as a much shorter time, so the two sources seem to contradict each other.

steps.title: רב חסדא: The משנה means 'after the after'
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the משנה's 'after' is a later stretch of time. It comes after the short time given in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: What does 'after' mean? 'After the after.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the contradiction. He says the משנה and the ברייתא are talking about two different stretches of time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's short time, reaching under the pillow, is the first 'after.' The משנה's longer time, getting out of bed and rinsing, is a further 'after' that comes later. Since they describe two different time frames, they do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: After the after: a time frame that comes after another time frame

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
What is 'after'? After the after.
phrases.notes: The משנה's time comes after the ברייתא's short 'after', so the משנה is talking about a later stage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַאי ״אַחַר״? אַחַר אַחַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the time frames: the two sources describe different stretches of time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources define the same 'after some time' and disagree about it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's 'after' is a later time frame that comes after the ברייתא's short one.

steps.title: A challenge to רב חסדא from the 'get down and rinse' definition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא from our משנה itself. The משנה teaches that blood found 'after some time' makes them impure because of doubt and free from a קרבן, and it defines that time as getting out of bed and rinsing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is taught about this: if blood was found on her cloth after some time, they are impure because of doubt and free from bringing a קרבן. What is 'after some time'? Enough time for her to get down from the bed and rinse her face.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב חסדא. It quotes a teaching that ties the 'get out of bed and rinse' time to the ruling 'impure because of doubt, free from a קרבן.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: That ruling belongs to the stage right after 'immediately,' when there is still a real doubt that she saw blood during relations. If the 'get down and rinse' time is that very next stage, it cannot be a later 'after the after' as רב חסדא said. The next step answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is taught about it: this opens a challenge from a teaching on the same case
Impure because of doubt
Free from bringing the חטאת offering
She rinses her 'face', a polite way of saying her private area

steps.confusionAlert: This step only asks the challenge. The answer, which defends רב חסדא, comes in the next step.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught about it:
If blood was found on hers after some time,
phrases.notes: 'Hers' means the checking cloth she used.

phrases.english: they are impure because of doubt, and free from the offering.
What is 'after some time'?
Enough time for her to get down from the bed
and rinse her face.
phrases.notes: 'Face' here is a polite way of saying her private area.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's answer from step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the משנה's 'after some time' is a later, 'after the after' stage. The challenge comes from the wording of the משנה itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'get down and rinse' time is linked to 'impure because of doubt, free from a קרבן.' That ruling belongs to the stage right after 'immediately,' not to a later third stage.

steps.title: The source is describing two different time frames
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the source from step 22. The short time, reaching under the pillow for a cloth, is 'after some time.' The longer time, getting out of bed and rinsing, is where רבי עקיבא and the חכמים argue.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: What is 'after some time'? Enough time for her to reach under the pillow or blanket, take a cloth and check. And the time it takes to get out of bed and rinse is the subject of the dispute between רבי עקיבא and the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge to רב חסדא. It says the source is not giving one definition. It is listing two separate time frames.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22 it looked like the source called the 'getting out of bed and rinsing' time 'after some time.' The גמרא now splits the source in two. The short pillow-reach time is 'after some time' (impure because of doubt, free from a קרבן). The longer rinsing time is a separate stage, where רבי עקיבא and the חכמים argue. This fits רב חסדא: the rinsing time comes after the short time.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it is saying'. The גמרא is rereading a source to explain what it really means
'After some time': blood found on the cloth a little while after relations
Pillow / blanket
A checking cloth used to check for blood
A dispute between sages

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as one long time frame. The גמרא is splitting it into two stages: the pillow-reach time first, then the rinsing time.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
What is "after some time"?
Enough time for her to reach out her hand
under the pillow or under the blanket
and take a cloth and check with it.
And as for enough time for her to get out of bed
and rinse her "face":
phrases.notes: "Face" here is a polite way of saying her private area.

phrases.english: that is a dispute between Rabbi Akiva and the Sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22 by rereading its source
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source as listing two separate time frames
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The source defines 'after some time' as the getting-out-of-bed-and-rinsing time, which goes against רב חסדא
steps.terutzMaskana: The source lists two stages: the short pillow-reach time is 'after some time,' and the rinsing time is the separate stage where רבי עקיבא and the חכמים argue

steps.title: But the dispute is about 'afterward'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects. The dispute between רבי עקיבא and the חכמים is about 'afterward,' meaning after the rinsing time. So how can the rinsing time itself be the subject of their dispute?
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches 'afterward'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rereading it just gave. The wording 'afterward' seems to place the dispute later than the rinsing time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute between רבי עקיבא and the חכמים is about 'afterward.' That word sounds like a time after the rinsing period. But step 23 said the rinsing period itself is the dispute. The two don't seem to match.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Afterward': the later stage of time where רבי עקיבא and the חכמים argue
'But it teaches!': a challenge from the exact wording of a source

phrases.english: But it teaches "afterward"!
phrases.notes: He means the word "afterward" at the point where רבי עקיבא and the חכמים argue. It sounds like it comes after the rinsing time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rereading of step 23 from the word 'afterward'
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 23's claim that the rinsing time is the subject of the dispute
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Afterward' implies a time after the rinsing time, so the dispute cannot be about the rinsing time itself

steps.title: The rinsing time is the 'afterward'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the rinsing time itself is what is called 'afterward.' It is 'after' the short pillow-reach time.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: this rinsing time is the 'afterward' about which רבי עקיבא and the חכמים argued.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection. 'Afterward' does not mean after the rinsing time. It means after the short time, and that later stage is the rinsing time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'afterward' is measured from the short pillow-reach time, not from the rinsing time. So the rinsing time is both the 'afterward' and the subject of the dispute. This keeps רב חסדא's two-stage picture in place.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagreed

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב חסדא's line: the short pillow-reach time is 'after some time' (impure because of doubt, free from a קרבן). The longer rinsing time is 'afterward,' where רבי עקיבא and the חכמים argue.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
And this is the "afterward"
phrases.notes: "This" means the time it takes to get out of bed and rinse.

phrases.english: about which Rabbi Akiva and the Sages disagreed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 24
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Afterward' means after the short pillow-reach time. That later stage is the rinsing time itself

steps.title: רב אשי: it is one time frame, depending on whether she holds the cloth
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי offers a different solution to the contradiction between the משנה and the ברייתא. Both describe the same amount of time. If the cloth is already in her hand, it is the getting-out-of-bed-and-rinsing time. If not, it is the time to reach under the pillow, take a cloth and check.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Both are one measure. If the cloth is in her hand, it is enough time to get out of bed and rinse. If the cloth is not in her hand, it is enough time to reach under the pillow or blanket, take a cloth and check.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new answer to the contradiction from step 20. He disagrees with רב חסדא's idea of two time frames.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said the משנה and the ברייתא describe two different stages of time. רב אשי says they describe the same length of time in two different situations. When she already holds the cloth, she has time to get out of bed and rinse. When she has to reach for it, the same time is used up reaching and checking.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This and that': both cases
A measure or amount, here an amount of time
The cloth is already in her hand

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not adding a third time frame. He is saying the two descriptions are the same amount of time, just used in different ways.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a second, competing way to settle the משנה and the ברייתא. The next step will challenge it.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
This and that are one measure.
If the cloth is in her hand:
enough time for her to get out of bed
and rinse her face.
If the cloth is not in her hand:
enough time for her to reach out her hand
under the pillow or under the blanket
and take a cloth and check with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי חַד שִׁיעוּרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the contradiction of step 20, instead of רב חסדא's answer
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two sources describe two different situations, not two different time frames
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא give two different lengths of time
steps.terutzMaskana: It is one length of time. Whether she already holds the cloth decides how it is described

steps.title: A challenge to רב אשי from what was asked in אושא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב אשי. It tells of רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק asking the חכמים in אושא what 'after some time' means. The actual content comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: What is 'after some time'? רבי אלעזר son of רבי צדוק asked this before the חכמים in אושא, and he said to them:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge against רב אשי. It starts quoting a ברייתא, and the rest of it continues in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מיתיבי' tells us a source is coming that seems to go against רב אשי's one-time-frame idea. Here we only get the opening: the question and who asked it. The point of the challenge will become clear once his words are quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: אושא, a town in the גליל where the חכמים gathered
Asked before (a group of חכמים)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
What is "after some time"?
This matter was asked by
Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok,
before the Sages in Usha,
and he said to them:
